notes:
EDITION: The 2026 MICHELIN Guide California is current. The selection was revealed at a ceremony at EVE in Downtown San Diego on Wednesday 2026-06-24. michelinmedia.com's post is dated June 24, 2026 and begins 'This evening...'; Fine Dining Lovers and SFist ('Wednesday night', published 2026-06-25) agree. The michelin.com page and PDF are dated 2026-06-26 (publication date, not the ceremony). The previous edition (2025) was revealed around 2025-06-25 (michelinmedia post dated June 25, 2025, 'Tonight').

SOURCES: Names, distinctions, Green Stars, 'new'/'promotion' flags and the full Bib list come from MICHELIN's own 2026 release on michelinmedia.com (article a1474; its tables are images, which I read) and the michelin.com PDF. Names use the release's spelling, with curly apostrophes changed to ASCII. Two names contain a pipe character: 'Pasta|Bar' and 'R|O-Rebel Omakase'.

ADDRESS WARNING: The michelin.com PDF's starred-restaurant table has a scrambled address column; for example it prints Californios at Providence's address and Lilo at a Napa address. The michelinmedia star-table images are correctly aligned and match each restaurant's 2025 address and the city given in the release text, so every star address here comes from the michelinmedia images. The Bib and Green Star tables match in both sources. Addresses are as MICHELIN printed them; the star tables omit 'California', the Bib and Green Star tables include it. I did not need any restaurant websites. Typo: the PDF and michelinmedia text print 'Headlsburg' for Troubadour.

COUNTS: 10 three-star, 13 two-star, 60 one-star (83 starred), 18 Green Stars, 117 Bib Gourmands. These match MICHELIN's own selection table, and the build script checks the totals. Recommended: michelinmedia says 321 (521 restaurants in total); the michelin.com PDF says 323 (523 in total). I used 321. RECOMMENDED LIST NOT INCLUDED: MICHELIN's release names only the 19 new 2026 Recommended restaurants and points to guide.michelin.com for the full 321/323 list, and that host is blocked for ClaudeBot. So only the count is recorded. Exception: the 5 Green-Star-only restaurants (Chez Panisse, Chi Spacca, Monte's, Pomet, Sierra Mar) are Recommended-level and are included in restaurants[] with distinction 'Recommended' and green_star true, because the task asks for every Green Star.

FIELDS: new_this_edition is true when any honor on that row is new in 2026: the 2 promotions to 3 Stars, Kato's promotion to 2 Stars, the 9 new 1 Stars (Seline and Troubadour are marked 'promotion' in the table but are among the 'nine restaurants' newly awarded One Star), the 3 new Green Stars (Six Test Kitchen's star is not new, only its Green Star) and the 7 new Bibs. Extra fields beyond the requested schema: 'change' (what changed, per MICHELIN), 'status_note' (MICHELIN's 'temporarily closed' marks), 'name_note' (Harbor House is printed as 'Harbor House Inn' in one michelinmedia image), and a top-level 'previous_edition' block.

CHANGES FROM 2025: These are computed by comparing MICHELIN's own 2025 list (michelinmedia a1409) with the 2026 list, with reasons only where a source states one. 13 restaurants that had 1 Star in 2025 are not starred in 2026; see previous_edition.stars_not_in_2026. SFist says The Shota, O' by Claude Le Tohic, Le Comptoir at Bar Crenn (which 'recently announced will be closing') and Kenzo lost their stars. LA Magazine says 715, Camphor and Morihiro lost theirs. Wikipedia footnotes give closures for Gucci Osteria (Eater LA, 2025-11-24), Shibumi (LA Times, 2025-07-14) and Uka (2025-12-10). For Gwen, Knife Pleat and Valle, no opened source says why. No 3-Star or 2-Star restaurant was demoted. Green Stars dropped: Le Comptoir at Bar Crenn, and The Restaurant at JUSTIN (it keeps its 1 Star). 14 Bibs from 2025 are not in 2026 (listed in previous_edition.bib_not_in_2026, reasons not stated). 'Pizzeria Bianco' was renamed 'Pizzeria Bianco Los Angeles'. The 2025 Bib table images show 124 rows, while MICHELIN's 2025 count says 123.

CLOSURES SINCE THE CEREMONY: These were checked through WhatNow's monthly closure roundups (LA July, August and September 2026; Bay Area September 2026), SFist's Michelin and closures tag pages, and targeted searches. Only Yank Sing's Rincon Center location (the MICHELIN-listed address) was found closed. The two Bibs already marked 'temporarily closed' by MICHELIN are recorded too. This check is not exhaustive: SF Chronicle, LA Times and Eater are blocked for ClaudeBot, and Axios returned 403. Other MICHELIN-recognized closures found are not in the 2026 starred or Bib lists (for example Prelude, a Recommended restaurant, closed 2026-09-19), so they are not in closed[].

OTHER FACTS FROM THE RELEASE: Special Awards were Exceptional Cocktails (Bar Team, Maria Isabel), Sommelier (Savannah Riedler, Lilo), Outstanding Service (Julianna Yang, Sons & Daughters) and Young Chef (Anna Sonenshein and Niki Vahle, Little Fish Melrose Hill).
